previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease and a history of diabetes and hypertension was admitted after his left arm dialysis fistula clotted. He underwent thrombectomy and angioplasty, but the fistula re-thrombosed. A tunneled dialysis catheter was placed in the left internal jugular vein for ongoing dialysis access. He experienced mild abdominal pain and constipation during admission, which resolved with conservative management. A chest X-ray showed the catheter tip in proper position and incidental nodular densities confirmed to be nipple shadows on repeat imaging. He completed a dialysis session before discharge and was sent home with instructions to follow up at the access clinic and continue outpatient dialysis via the catheter.
problems: Other complications due to renal dialysis device, implant, and graft
